To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the cross section contributions from two-nuclear diffraction events are small, (2) the cross sections from two-nuclear inelastic stripping and diffraction events are approximately the same size and (3) the measured two-nucleon removal cross sections are smaller than predicted by the shell model.

the contributions of two nucleon diffraction to two nucleon knockout reactions at intermediate energies are small and that the suppression of the shell model strength is consistent for all five reactions studied.

(1) the cross sections of two-neutron and two-proton knockout reactions are suppressed, (2) the suppression factors for two-neutron and for two-proton removal are the same, and (3) these suppression factors are approximately 0.5.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a unified theory of nuclear reactions, based on a microscopic description of the structure of the colliding nuclei and the reaction mechanism.
the development and application of a theoretical framework for the description of two-neutron (proton) knockout reactions at intermediate energies (100-400 MeV per nucleton).
the application of the shell model to the description of the structure of nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the suppression of shell model strength is a universal phenomenon in intermediate energy two-nuclear knockout reactions.
the two-nucleon cross-section data are in reasonable agreement with the theory, but the shell-model transition strengths must be suppressed to account for the data.
the two-nucleon cross sections are suppressed by a factor of approximately 0.5, but the evidence is not yet conclusive, and further work is needed to clarify the situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the suppression factors are independent of the incident energy and of the reaction type.

the two-nucleon shell-model strengths are suppressed by approximately a factor of two, with the suppression being due to both a reduction in the spectroscopic amplitudes of the ground and excited states and the inclusion of diffraction contributions.
the suppression of the shell-model strength for two-nucleon removal reactions is of order 1/2, with a small additional contribution arising from the diffraction dissociation mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shell-model strength suppression factor, Rs, for two-nucleon knock out reactions, is approximately the same as for single-nucleon knock-out reactions.
the shell model is still the best way to describe the structure of the ground state wave function, and that the suppression factors are the same for the different reactions.
